text: Unlike Egret-3, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Siskin-3 is the Tessera team. Nobody should assume the owner of Siskin-3 applies to Egret-3, the owner differs.

Unlike Plover-3, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Egret-3 is March 7, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Egret-3 applies to Plover-3, the retirement date differs.
Questions about Heron-8 start with its owner, the Tessera team; they triage anything filed against it.
Wren-3 runs in the Osaka datacenter, next to its database. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Egret-3 is implemented in Rust; the language was chosen for its tooling.
Plover-3 listens on port 2519; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Bittern-4 enforces a rate limit of 3050 requests per minute per caller.
Bittern-4 has one owner, the Harbor team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
All instances of Siskin-3 live in the datacenter at Dublin. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Questions about Egret-3 start with its owner, the Compass team; they triage anything filed against it.
Plan around the retirement date of Heron-8: October 7, 2027 is when it goes dark.
Heron-8 enforces a rate limit of 2150 requests per minute per caller.
Bittern-4 is implemented in Elixir; the language was chosen for its tooling. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Rosa Marchetti is on the pager rotation of Bittern-4 this month, with a deputy as backup.

Unlike Bittern-4, whose pager rotation is handled elsewhere, the pager rotation of Siskin-3 is Jolene Pemberton. Nobody should assume the pager rotation of Siskin-3 applies to Bittern-4, the pager rotation differs.
Pages from Egret-3 land on the pager rotation of Priya Pemberton before anyone else.

Unlike Siskin-3, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Plover-3 is the Tallinn datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Plover-3 applies to Siskin-3, the datacenter differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
Nadia Halvorsen is on the pager rotation of Heron-8 this month, with a deputy as backup.
The pager rotation for Plover-3 is run by Yusuf Abernathy; alerts page them first. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Bittern-4, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Egret-3 is 150 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Egret-3 applies to Bittern-4, the rate limit differs.
Plan around the retirement date of Wren-3: January 10, 2028 is when it goes dark.
Unlike Heron-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Plover-3 is the Harbor team. Nobody should assume the owner of Plover-3 applies to Heron-8, the owner differs.
Unlike Heron-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Siskin-3 is 6082. Nobody should assume the port of Siskin-3 applies to Heron-8, the port differs.

Unlike Heron-8, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Plover-3 is February 11, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Plover-3 applies to Heron-8, the retirement date differs.
The owner of Wren-3 is the Lattice team, and every change to Wren-3 goes through their review.
Wren-3 was granted a budget of $2980k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Wren-3 listens on port 4373; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
Siskin-3 reaches its retirement date on October 10, 2028, so every consumer has to migrate before then. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Wren-3, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Bittern-4 is $1530k. Nobody should assume the budget of Bittern-4 applies to Wren-3, the budget differs.
For Heron-8 the port is 5963. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
